# No test tier asserts the App Worker console is clean

> ⚠️ **CORRECTED before any work started — my original prescription was impossible, and I found it while implementing it.**
>
> The first version of this ticket proposed a gate in the `neuralLink` fixture teardown and claimed it *"would have turned #18546 red in CI exactly as configured today."* **That is false.** `fixtures.mjs:48` hard-requires `NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT` for the `neuralLink` fixture, and the four CI-selected Workstation specs contain **zero** `neuralLink` references — they take `{page}` or `{neo, page}`. A gate living in that fixture can never run in CI.
>
> I had measured that those four specs are selected and that they boot the Workstation. I never checked whether they could use the fixture I was putting the gate in. The measurements below all hold; the prescription built on them did not.
>
> The problem statement survives and is in fact **worse** than originally stated — see *The real constraint*. The fix below replaces the original, and the original ACs are struck.

## Context

#18551 broke every Workstation viewport vdom sync on `dev` and shipped with **24/24 CI checks green**. @tobiu found it by opening the app; he then asked whether we need more unit or e2e tests.

We do not, at least not first. #18546 had a dedicated arm on **each** half of the change, and the Workstation has 34 e2e specs. The regression was invisible for reasons no additional spec of the same kind would fix.

## The Problem

**(1) The failure is caught, so nothing can fail on it.** `src/mixin/VdomLifecycle.mjs:378` swallows a failed update into a log:

```javascript
VDomUpdate.hasPromiseCallbacks(me.id) || console.error('vdom update failed', me.id, err);
```

That is deliberate and the comment explains why. The consequence is that no `pageerror` fires and no promise rejects unhandled.

**(2) The log lands where no CI-runnable test can read it.** `src/worker/App.mjs:397` wraps `console[log|warn|error|info]` and `:445` hooks `globalThis.onerror`. **Both route exclusively to `Neo.ai?.Client`** — the Neural Link bridge. `original.apply(console, args)` still fires, but that writes to the SharedWorker's own console context, which the page never sees.

**(3) Most of the tier does not run in CI.** `NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT` is set in no workflow, and `playwright.config.e2e.mjs:80` applies `testIgnore: externalBrainTestIgnore`. Measured with `--list` under a CI-shaped environment:

| | count |
|---|---|
| e2e spec files in the repo | 106 |
| **selected** | **20** (62 tests) |
| Workstation specs in the repo | 34 |
| **Workstation selected** | **4** |

Known and documented — `.github/workflows/test-e2e.yml:281` states *"Specs removed by testIgnore are dropped without warning."*

**(4) Nothing asserts the worker console is clean.** Across 106 e2e spec files, **exactly one** asserts the blanket form: `e2e/rendering/ContextMenuNL.spec.mjs:204`, `expect(await app.getConsoleLogs('error')).toEqual([])`. Separately, of the **47** `page.on('pageerror', …)` handler sites, **23 are pure prints** that write to stdout and fail nothing.

## The real constraint

The four checks that decide the shape:

| | |
|---|---|
| `app.getConsoleLogs()` lives on | the `neuralLink` fixture (`fixtures.mjs:660`) |
| `neuralLink` requires | `NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT`, absolute, or it throws (`fixtures.mjs:48`) |
| `ContextMenuNL` — the one blanket assertion — takes | `{page, neuralLink}` → **not selected in CI** |
| the 4 CI-selected Workstation specs take | `{page}` / `{neo, page}` → **cannot reach `getConsoleLogs`** |

So the ability to observe App Worker errors is **coupled to the private Brain checkout**, and everything that runs in CI is on the other side of that boundary. This is not a missing assertion; it is a missing *channel*. Adding assertions anywhere cannot fix it.

## The Fix

**Give App Worker errors a main-thread path, so observing them needs no Brain.**

The worker already has a message channel to Main. In `development` only, and for `error` level only, forward the intercepted console output and the `onerror` payload to the main thread, which re-emits it there. `page.on('console')` and `page.on('pageerror')` then see it — both available to **every** spec, with no fixture dependency and no Brain checkout.

This is worth doing on its own merits, independent of testing: a Neo app's errors currently vanish into a SharedWorker console that a developer has to know to go looking for. Making them surface in the page console is what every non-worker framework already gives you.

The gate then becomes a per-test check in the **shared** fixture on `page`, which all 20 CI-selected specs already take.

Deliberately not chosen: attaching a CDP session to the `shared_worker` target from the harness. It needs no engine change, but it is Chromium-only harness plumbing that helps no human developer, and it leaves the underlying invisibility in place.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1 — App Worker `error` output reaches the main thread in `development`.** Forwarded from both interception points (`worker/App.mjs:397` console wrap and `:445` `onerror`), carrying message and stack. Positive control: an error raised in the worker appears in the page console; a `log`-level call does not.
- [ ] **AC-2 — no behaviour change outside `development`.** Positive control: with the environment set to `production`, the forward does not run and no channel traffic is produced.
- [ ] **AC-3 — the gate lives in the shared fixture on `page`**, so it applies to every spec including the 20 CI-selected ones, with no per-spec assertion and no `neuralLink` dependency.
- [ ] **AC-4 — red-first against the real regression, under today's CI selection.** On a base carrying #18551's defect, at least one **currently-CI-selected** Workstation spec fails *through the gate*. `dev` carries that defect until #18552 merges, so this control is a live regression rather than a synthetic one — capture it before that lands.
- [ ] **AC-5 — the noise floor is measured and published before the default is chosen.** Per-spec `error` inventory across the CI-selected set, in the PR body. Zero floor ⇒ gate defaults on. Otherwise it lands with a **named** allowlist, each entry citing spec and error, and the allowlist is this ticket's residual.
- [ ] **AC-6 — opt-out is per-test and reasoned.** A spec waives the gate only by naming the expected error. Positive control: a test that deliberately triggers a worker error passes with the waiver and fails without it.
- [ ] **AC-7 — no print-only error handler survives in the CI-selected set.** The 23 `console.error('BROWSER JS ERROR:', …)` handlers become assertions or are deleted, scoped to the 20 selected files. A handler that logs and cannot fail is a false guard — the same defect class that let #18551 through.

## Out of Scope

- **Making the Brain-gated 86 run in CI.** Needs the private `neo-agent-brain` checkout on the runner — infra and credentials, a different owner. Recorded as the reason the fix must not depend on `neuralLink`, and deliberately not bundled. Note this ticket now *reduces* the pressure on it: the worker console stops being Brain-only.
- **Changing `executeVdomUpdate`'s catch.** Logging rather than throwing is the documented intent. The gap is that nothing can *read* the log.
- **Forwarding `log`/`warn`/`info` levels.** Error only; the rest is volume with no gate attached.
- **`VDom.syncVdomState:451` mapping before filtering `removeDom`.** Recorded on #18551; unchanged.
- **The unit tier's fixture-vs-runtime problem.** #18551's post-mortem found two false guards built on config objects rather than materialised components (@neo-opus-grace: *"calls production code ≠ exercises the runtime object"*). Wants a skill, not a harness change.

## Avoided Traps

- **"Add more Workstation e2e specs."** There are 34; 30 do not run in CI, and the 4 that do were green through the whole defect.
- **Asserting on a specific error string.** What the Workstation specs already do (`'Dock projection failed'`), and why an unrelated error passed. A gate must be blanket or it only catches errors someone already predicted.
- **Putting the gate where the capability already exists.** The original error in this ticket. `getConsoleLogs` was the obvious home precisely *because* it already worked — in the half of the tier that never runs.

## Decision Record impact

`none`. Adds a development-only diagnostic channel and a test-harness gate; changes no runtime contract.

## Related

- #18551 / #18552 — the regression that motivated this, and the fix
- #18545 / #18546 — where both false guards were introduced
- @neo-opus-vega's `defect-note` on the CI-shaped tier reporting window chrome as 0x0 — likely the same configuration surfacing differently

### @neo-opus-ada - 2026-09-09T18:21:08Z

## Split: AC-1 and AC-2 moved to #18556 (PR #18557). This ticket now starts at the gate.

The corrected fix above had two halves — a **channel** (mirror App-Worker errors to the main thread) and a **gate** (fail a test that mirrors one). Only the channel is provable today, so it went to #18556 and shipped there. Everything below is what remains here.

The channel is verified: with the topology-bar defect reinstated locally, a Workstation boot puts `App Worker: … Component not found for id: neo-component-34` in the **page** console, with no Brain checkout and no Neural Link. So the gate is no longer blocked by an unreadable signal. It is blocked by something narrower.

## What blocks the gate: no page-only way to provoke a worker error

I wrote the gate — a `page` fixture override collecting `App Worker: `-prefixed console errors, with a `test.use({allowedWorkerErrors: '<reason>'})` waiver — and then removed it, because **I could not make it fail in CI.** A guard whose red path is unexercised is the defect this ticket exists to fix, so shipping it would have been the joke telling itself.

Two attempts, both recorded so nobody spends the cycle again:

| attempt | why it failed |
|---|---|
| `neo.createComponent` a container, plant an unresolvable `componentId` in its vdom | the container **never mounts**, so no vnode sync runs and `getVdom` is never reached. *Mounted* is the load-bearing word |
| corrupt a **mounted** component (id read off the DOM, since Neo stamps component ids as DOM ids), then `page.setViewportSize` to provoke a re-render | still silent. `VdomLifecycle.mjs:378` only **logs** when `hasPromiseCallbacks(me.id)` is false, and an awaited RMA call parks a promise — so the failure rejects into the caller instead |

And the engine offers no public path either, which is the part worth knowing:

- the App-Worker `remote` manifest exposes `createNeoInstance`, `destroyNeoInstance`, `fireEvent`, `getConfigs`, `getWorkerId`, `loadModule`, `moveComponent`, `setConfigs`, `setGlobalConfig` — none of which raise a worker-side `console.error`
- `destroyNeoInstance` routes through `parent.remove()`, the path that splices `items` **and** `getVdomItemsRoot().cn` together, so it cannot leave an orphan stub

That last row is reassuring about the engine and unhelpful here: **the only way this repo is known to produce an orphan stub is a bug.**

## What the gate still needs

- [ ] **A page-only trigger for an App-Worker error** — a fire-and-forget update that fails. The discriminating requirement is `hasPromiseCallbacks(me.id) === false`, so an awaited RMA call cannot be it. Candidates not yet tried: an interaction-driven re-render on an already-corrupted subtree, or a deliberate error inside a component lifecycle hook loaded via `loadModule`.
- [ ] **The `'App Worker: '` prefix coupling.** The mirror writes it in the browser; the gate matches it in Node. They cannot share an import — `src/worker/App.mjs` is browser-only — so the coupling has to be held by the end-to-end control above, not by a constant. Until that control exists the prefix is unguarded on both sides.
- [ ] AC-5 (noise floor), AC-6 (waiver control), AC-7 (the 23 print-only `pageerror` handlers) carry over unchanged.

`Depends-on: #18556.`

## CORRECTED — the blocker I stated twice is false outside `app`. @neo-opus-vega measured it.

This ticket's redirected fix says the gate stays blocked because **no page-only trigger for a worker error exists**. I wrote that in the body, repeated it in the #18557 PR, and repeated it again in #18566's Out of Scope.

It is true for the **App** worker. It is **false for the other four**, and I verified @neo-opus-vega's finding from source rather than taking it:

```
Data.mjs:237   async loadModule({path}) { … catch (e) {
                   console.error(`Data Worker: Failed to load module ${path}`, e);
                   return {success: false, path, error: e.message}   ← RECEIPT, no throw
               } }
RemoteMethodAccess.onRemoteMethod
               pkg    = Neo.ns(msg.remoteClassName)
               method = pkg[msg.remoteMethod]                        ← NO caller verification
```

So the main thread can invoke it directly:

```js
await Neo.worker.Manager.promiseMessage('data', {
    action: 'remoteMethod', remoteClassName: 'Neo.worker.Data',
    remoteMethod: 'loadModule', data: [{path: 'no/such/module/at/all'}]
});
```

Her receipt at merged `d080a73813`, on `/examples/stateProvider/multiWindow/`:

```
RECEIPT      = {"success":false,"path":"no/such/module/at/all","error":"Unsupported module root: …"}
PAGE_CONSOLE = []
```

**Four sites of this shape:** `Data.mjs:158`, `:214`, `:237`, `Canvas.mjs:92`.

## Why this is better than merely unblocking

The trigger is **benign** — no throw, no unhandled rejection — and it **returns a receipt**, which gives the arm an **independent oracle that the operation ran**. That is what both #18556 and #18557 lacked: their arms could only assert an *absence*, and an absence is satisfied identically by a working mirror and by no mirror at all. Here `PAGE_CONSOLE=[]` beside a successful receipt is the defect demonstrated live rather than inferred, and after the hoist the same arm shows the line appearing. **Red-first, presence-proven, page-only.**

That also discharges the reason I refused to ship the gate in #18557: *"a guard whose red path is unexercised is the defect this ticket exists to fix."* The red path is now exercisable.

## What my error was

I checked the **App worker's** remote manifest, found nothing that raises a worker-side `console.error`, and wrote *"the App-Worker remote manifest exposes none"* — accurately — and then generalised it to *"no page-only trigger exists"*. The population I measured was one worker; the claim covered five. Same shape as the rest of my misses today: the measurement held, the claim about what it covered ran ahead.

## Scope now

- The **control** lives in #18566, where @neo-opus-vega is writing it as the red-first arm *before* the hoist, which is the right place — the mirror has to exist for a non-App worker before a gate can assert on it.
- **This ticket's remaining scope is the gate itself** (fail a test whose worker mirrored an error), plus AC-5 noise floor, AC-6 waiver control and AC-7 the print-only handlers. It is no longer blocked on a missing trigger; it is sequenced behind #18566.
- The **App worker still has no page-only trigger.** That half of my claim stands, and it is why the gate's first control will be a Data-worker one.

### @neo-opus-ada - 2026-09-12T22:14:04Z

## CORRECTED — the App worker does have a page-only trigger; I measured one

My [previous comment](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/18554#issuecomment-5608544017) ended: *"The App worker still has no page-only trigger. That half of my claim stands."* It does not stand.

### The measurement

Portal served from a worktree at `dev@8cab26fcf8` (plain static server, headless Chromium, no Brain checkout, no Neural Link). Open `#/learn/guides/uibuildingblocks/DockLayoutsPanes` and scroll each `.neo-h2` / `.neo-h3` into view in turn. The **page** console receives, at steps 1 through 5:

```text
App Worker: TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'split')
```

It arrives through the mirror #18567 generalised. The same error fires on a second learn route, 2 runs of 2. A harness that scrolled only to each page's diagrams saw it on one route and not on the other — the scroll path decides whether it is observed at all.

### Why it is the trigger this ticket asked for

The chain is `App#onDomEvent` → `DomEvent#fire` → `apps/portal/view/learn/MainContainerController.mjs#onIntersect` → `selectionModel.select(list.store.get(parseInt(recordId)))` → `select(null)` → `SectionsList#getItemRecordId(null)` → `null.split`. No RMA call sits in it, so no promise is parked and `hasPromiseCallbacks` never swallows the failure: a fire-and-forget App-worker error, provoked from the page alone. That is the discriminating requirement the gate's control section names.

### Why it is not the permanent control

It is a defect. The learn controller passes an unguarded `store.get` result to `select`, while `apps/portal/view/news/tickets/MainContainerController.mjs` guards both the id and the record before selecting. Fixed, it stops being a trigger. So it can serve as the gate's **red** half against today's base, and a benign App-worker trigger with its own receipt — the property that made the Data-worker `loadModule` control good — is still open.

The pairing it suggests: land the gate with this as its red-first arm, then the one-guard fix turns that arm green in the same change. That also demonstrates this ticket's thesis on shipped content: every scrolled learn guide throws in the App Worker today, and no tier noticed.

**Not measured:** why a record id misses the store. The sections list's `<li>` items also match `.neo-h2` / `.neo-h3` and carry no `data-record-id`, while `src/app/content/Component.mjs` observes exactly those selectors — but I did not verify whether that observation is scoped to the content component. Treat that as a lead, not the cause.

### @neo-opus-ada - 2026-09-14T19:20:50Z

**A gap in the channel this gate would stand on — found from source today, not yet measured at runtime.**

The worker→page mirror (`src/worker/Base.mjs`, since the #18556/#18567 work) forwards two things: `console.error` through `interceptConsole`, and `globalThis.onerror`. It does not forward **unhandled promise rejections**. The engine's only `unhandledrejection` listener, in `src/Neo.mjs`, calls `preventDefault()` for `Neo.isDestroyed` and nothing else, so every other rejection takes the browser default. In a SharedWorker that default is the worker's own inspector context, which never reaches `console.error` — and the portal runs `useSharedWorkers: true` in `development`.

**Why this matters for the gate:** #18704 — the unbuilt `dist/highlight` bundle, fixed in PR #18706 — is exactly that class. A failed dynamic `import()` rejects `Markdown#render()` from an async config hook, so no guide with a code fence rendered on any hosted runner, silently. A gate that only reads today's mirror would have stayed green through it.

**So the gate lane widens by one interception point.** Forward `unhandledrejection` reasons (message and stack) on the same dev-only SharedWorker path and prefix, excluding `Neo.isDestroyed`. - 2026-09-15T00:15:21Z @neo-opus-ada referenced in commit `b4febd1` - "fix(component): a silently destroyed child stays in its parent's stored vnode unnamed, until the next update (#18554)

destroy(true, true) removed a child from its parent's vdom but left its
{componentId} reference in the parent's stored vnode. Until the parent's next
update landed, a strict walk through that vnode, such as an ancestor flight's
landing, threw "Component not found". A plain container reproduces it.

component.Base#destroy now unlinks the reference once the child has left the
registry: the node stays as the vnode the child last rendered, so the parent's
next update still removes it, or diffs a newcomer with the same id against it.
VdomLifecycle#syncVnodeTree unlinks at the landing boundary as well. It used to
prune, which left a retired child's DOM node in place for good.
util.VNode#pruneRetiredReferences becomes unlinkRetiredReferences.

grid.Body#createRowPool is back to retiring rows one at a time, now through
destroy(true, true), which grid.Row#destroy forwards. Its own DOM removal,
transport catch and prune are gone."

holds: `destroy(true, …)` per retired row does two things the contraction does not
need. Its parent-vdom edit is redundant — `createRowPool` rebuilds `cn` from the
surviving pool immediately after the loop — and its stored-vnode walk runs once per
row over a tree that still holds the whole pool.

retired set in one `VNodeUtil.unlinkRetiredReferences` call, the shape the map
argument was built for. Measured on a 205 -> 20 contraction over 10 columns, three
runs each, precondition-guarded so both shapes start from a populated vnode:
27.3-34.4 ms -> 2.6-4.2 ms, 185 -> 0 parent-vdom edits, 189,440 -> 2,036 node
descents. Same end state: the stored vnode stays walkable and 20 references survive.

`Pooling.spec` and the non-grid `RaceCondition.spec` arms are unchanged and green,
17 of 17.

declines it, so a caught-and-logged error in a dedicated worker passed the gate.

workerErrors now also records each error ConsoleMessage#worker attributes to a
worker, named from its script the way the mirror names a line (App.mjs gives
"App Worker: "), so one waiver reads in either mode. WorkerErrorGate.spec runs
its worker arms once per channel, on an app whose mode it asserts, and reads
the receipt from either reply shape.

* fix(ai): the AI client's bridge give-up is its warning, not the socket's error (#18554)

With the gate reading dedicated workers, RowPinning.spec failed on
"App Worker: Max reconnection attempts reached". Apps that set useAiClient
start the Neural Link client, which gives up after five attempts when no
bridge listens, about 15 s after boot, so only long arms outlive it.
ai.Client#onSocketError already reports an absent bridge as a warning; the
give-up was the one path still logged as an error, by the socket itself.

data.connection.WebSocket now fires reconnect_failed with a handled flag and
logs the error only when no owner sets it. ai.Client warns and sets it. A
give-up nobody handles is still an error, whether or not someone listened.

* refactor(data): the socket's give-up event is named like every other Neo event (#18554)

`reconnect_failed` was the only snake_case event name fired anywhere in src/, apps/ or
examples/, against 135 camelCase fire() sites. It shipped unlistened in v11.18.0 (#8177);
this branch adds its first consumer and its payload contract, so the name is settled here
rather than carried into that contract. No consumer exists in any neomjs checkout.

Co-Authored-By: Ada <neo-opus-4-7@neomjs.com>

* perf(grid): a shrinking row pool leaves the stored vnode in one walk, not one per row (#18554)

@tobiu challenged the bulk retirement the RA-1 repair introduced, and the challenge
holds: `destroy(true, …)` per retired row does two things the contraction does not
need. Its parent-vdom edit is redundant — `createRowPool` rebuilds `cn` from the
surviving pool immediately after the loop — and its stored-vnode walk runs once per
row over a tree that still holds the whole pool.

The contraction now retires rows with a plain `destroy()` and unlinks the whole
retired set in one `VNodeUtil.unlinkRetiredReferences` call, the shape the map
argument was built for. Measured on a 205 -> 20 contraction over 10 columns, three
runs each, precondition-guarded so both shapes start from a populated vnode:
27.3-34.4 ms -> 2.6-4.2 ms, 185 -> 0 parent-vdom edits, 189,440 -> 2,036 node
descents. Same end state: the stored vnode stays walkable and 20 references survive.

`Pooling.spec` and the non-grid `RaceCondition.spec` arms are unchanged and green,
17 of 17.
